analysis.investment_thesis: Dynamatic Technologies fails the Magic Formula on both key metrics: Earnings Yield is a dismal ~2.1% (EBIT ₹160 Cr / EV ~₹7,554 Cr) against a 12%+ threshold, and ROCE of 8.96% is well below the 20%+ standard for a high-quality business. At 150x trailing P/E with flat revenue over 9 years, the stock offers no margin of safety.
key_strengths: Diversified across aerospace, automotive, and hydraulics — reduces single-sector risk
Consistent positive operating cash flow (5/5 years), averaging ~₹120 Cr/year
Debt reduction visible: borrowings down from ₹743 Cr (2020) to ₹571 Cr (2025)
key_risks: Revenue stagnant/declining: 9-year CAGR of -0.7%, from ₹1,490 Cr (2016) to ₹1,404 Cr (2025)
Capital returns are far too low for the price: ROCE 8.96%, ROE 6.21% — barely above cost of capital
Valuation is extreme: EV/EBITDA of 58x and P/E of 150x leave zero room for error or disappointment
red_flags: 2024 net profit of ₹122 Cr was massively distorted by ₹105 Cr in 'Other Income' (likely one-time asset sale); normalized profit reverts to ~₹43 Cr
Earnings yield of ~2.1% (EBIT/EV) is among the worst possible scores on the Magic Formula — 6x below minimum threshold
Free cash flow collapsing: FCF fell from ₹168 Cr (2020) to ₹22 Cr (2024), recovering only partially to ₹78 Cr in 2025
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Dynamatic Technologies produces a near-failing grade on both axes. Earnings Yield = EBIT ₹160 Cr / EV (~₹7,015.9 Cr market cap + ₹571 Cr debt − ₹33 Cr cash = ₹7,554 Cr) = **2.1%** — the Formula demands at least 12%. Return on Capital, proxied by the reported ROCE of **8.96%**, is barely above a savings account rate and well below the 20% minimum for a "good business." The gross margin of 48% looks optically appealing, but it collapses to 7.2% at the operating level, indicating heavy overhead and depreciation drag — the hallmark of a capital-intensive business that struggles to earn its cost of capital.

The 2024 earnings spike (₹122 Cr net profit) is a textbook red flag: it was driven by ₹105 Cr of "Other Income," likely a one-time asset disposal. Strip that out and normalized earnings are ~₹43 Cr, which is what FY2025 confirmed. At ₹43 Cr of earnings against a ₹7,016 Cr market cap, the stock trades at a staggering ~163x normalized earnings. The Magic Formula is a systematic screener that would rank this stock in the absolute bottom decile — expensive AND mediocre returns. There is no variant perception here that changes the math.
